title: Is Google Gemini Argon as good as the competitors for coding?
author: Vegetable_Voice_2044
selftext:
I have been using Google Gemini pro, and then argon since it's release as my only ai tool for code generation, reviews, and refactoring. But it seems like every post I see in this reddit channel is about anything but Gemini.

I do not have the time to tinker with all of them, so I have to ask... Am I using an inferior tool, or is it just less popular?

I use it exclusively for code work, as all of my art assets are purchased low poly assets from Sytny.

comments.author: boxing-boxing
comments.body:
Yes, google is far behind unless they’ve had significant advancements recently.

Claude opus 5.5 is winning in terms of agentic coding right now

comments.author: Sirramza
comments.body: No is not, but its ok for small projects

comments.author: phantomimp
comments.body: Gemini Argon wins at creativity and understanding your intentions, it loses however in coding capabilities. Imo the best combo ist planning with Gemini Argon and implementing with Opus 5.5 for the best results.

replies.author: Wide-Bobcat-3723
replies.body: I agree with Argon winning at creativity and reading your mind but it's not that far behind in coding. I also think it blows Opus5.5 out if the water in terms of 3D animation coding.

replies.author: phantomimp
replies.body: Interesting that you say that. I have not tried it for 3D Games yet.

comments.author: strange_username58
comments.body: It's not as good as opus 5.5, but it's good enough

comments.author: shuozhe
comments.body: It's different, get the job done, reads a lot of code.. but it's just very few token compared to claude

comments.author: Fuzzzy420
comments.body: To expensive, not for coding but debugging and planning.

comments.author: _Dingaloo
comments.body:
apx as good in my experience, but more expensive and not quite as good in key areas. Not really noticably worse in 99% of applications. And google's way of planning etc and managing AI workflows rivals claudes. Blows gpt out of the water. 

But purely for its agent's skill, it's nothing crazy or better than what's already out there, and it costs too much.

I still use 3.8 flash for most things when I use gemini. Still feels like the best efficiency model out there. Argon needs work before it gets there. I do think argon will get there though, google is playing the long game and I would be very surprised if soon argon or a similar high thinking model wasn't more efficient than all competition. iirc they used a completely different training method that sets them apart a lot, and for such a new method it sounds promising, especially since it's first public iteration is already so competitive

comments.author: romansamurai
comments.body: Gemini was far behind the main competitors (ChatGPT and Claude). Like far behind. But it’s better now with argon. However given their history I see no reason for me or anyone else to switch from something that works incredibly well to test it out.

comments.author: Double_Suggestion385
comments.body: No, it's worse than Sonnet 5.5 and much worse than Opus and Fable.

comments.author: Soul_Mate_4ever
comments.body: Anything Gemini related is usually bard, minus the r.

comments.author: Gelinhir
comments.body: I did a game for myself and it felt really good. The result was impressive
